network_dim: LoRA rank (dimension of low-rank matrices). Higher = more expressive but more VRAM. Typical: 8–64.
network_alpha: LoRA scaling factor. Effective scale = alpha / dim. When alpha == dim, scale is 1.0. Lower alpha = more conservative updates.
lokr_full_factor: LoKr full-matrix mode (official LyCORIS full_matrix). Keeps both w1 and w2 full; LyCORIS forces the effective scale to 1.
use_loha: Enable LoHa (Low-rank Hadamard product, LyCORIS backend): deltaW = (w1a@w1b) ⊙ (w2a@w2b) * (alpha/rank). Two rank-r factor pairs give an effective rank up to r² at 2x the LoRA-r parameter count. Saves canonical hada_* keys; channel scaling is auto-disabled.
network_module: Python module path for the LoRA network implementation.
use_timestep_mask: Enable T-LoRA: effective rank varies with denoising timestep via power-law schedule. Full rank at high noise, reduced at low noise.
use_ortho: Enable OrthoLoRA: SVD-based orthogonal parameterization of the update matrix (linear layers only). Regularizes toward structured updates; saved as plain LoRA via thin SVD at checkpoint time.
use_moe_style: MoE expert layout: 'shared_A' (HydraLoRA — one shared lora_down + N per-expert lora_up heads), 'independent_A' (FeRA — N fully-independent down/up pairs), or false (no MoE). Produces a *_moe.safetensors sibling for router-live inference; requires cache_llm_adapter_outputs=true.
route_per_layer: If true, each layer owns its own router (per-layer routing). If false, a single network-level GlobalRouter broadcasts gate weights to every routed module.
use_repa: Enable REPA v2: a training-only auxiliary loss aligning a mid-block DiT feature to cached PE-Spatial patch tokens (default encoder pe_spatial) at every sampled σ. Improves representation quality without changing inference. Requires {stem}_anima_pe_spatial.safetensors sidecars (run preprocess-pe). Tune via repa_mode / repa_weight / repa_layer.
repa_target_dog: DoG (difference-of-Gaussians) band-pass on the REPA target before the relational Gram match — strips the low-frequency band (smooth global composition that otherwise dominates the Gram and persists into high σ) so alignment focuses on mid/high-frequency structure. Generalizes the older spatial_norm DC-removal and **replaces** it when on (mutually exclusive). Pure target-side preprocessing: a byte-identical no-op when off, so it can't regress a non-DoG run. **Recommended on whenever `use_repa` is enabled** (Phase-0 bench beat spatial_norm on all 3 content axes; character quality peaks at `repa_dog_sigma1_div=16`). Relational mode only — ignored if `repa_mode` isn't relational.
router_source: Routing signal: 'sigma' (sinusoidal embedding of the denoising timestep), 'fei' (mean-pooled rank features from preceding LoRA modules), or 'pooled_text' (pooled T5 caption embedding).
num_experts: HydraLoRA expert count. More experts = more capacity but more VRAM and slower training. Typical: 2–8.
balance_loss_weight: HydraLoRA load-balancing loss weight. Discourages router collapse onto a single expert. Typical: 0.01.
balance_loss_warmup_ratio: Fraction of training steps to hold the balance loss at 0 before activating it. Lets the router specialize first, then switches the penalty on to stop further collapse of a diverged router. 0.0 disables the warmup. Typical: 0.3–0.5.
sigma_feature_dim: Sinusoidal σ feature dimension fed into the σ-router bias MLP. Typical: 128.
router_targets: Regex over layer names — only matching Linears participate in routed adaptation (Hydra MoE leaves + σ / FEI feature concatenation share the same scope). Typical: '.*(mlp\.layer[12])$' to confine MoE to the FFN sublayers.
per_bucket_balance_weight: Extra per-σ-bucket load-balance penalty, scaled by balance_loss_weight. Encourages routing diversity within each timestep bucket. Typical: 0.3.
num_sigma_buckets: Number of timestep buckets used for per-bucket balance accounting. Typical: 3 (low / mid / high noise).
specialize_experts_by_sigma_buckets: Hard-partition the expert pool into σ-bands: each timestep bucket only routes to its assigned experts. Forces specialization on top of the soft σ-router bias. Pairs with sigma_bucket_boundaries.
sigma_bucket_boundaries: Custom σ-bucket edges, length = num_sigma_buckets + 1, monotone 0.0 → 1.0. Defaults to uniform linspace(0, 1, N+1) when omitted. Example: [0.0, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0].
network_args: Extra kwargs passed to the network module. For postfix: list of 'key=value' strings (e.g., 'mode=cond', 'splice_position=end_of_sequence', 'cond_hidden_dim=256'). Pick a Variant to auto-fill.
min_rank: Minimum active rank when T-LoRA timestep masking is enabled. At the lowest-noise timesteps, rank drops to this value.
alpha_rank_scale: Scale alpha proportionally when T-LoRA reduces rank, keeping effective learning rate stable across timesteps.
network_train_unet_only: Train only the DiT (U-Net). Text encoder weights are frozen. Recommended for most LoRA training.
network_weights: Path to a pre-trained adapter checkpoint to warm-start from, e.g. output/ckpt/xxx.safetensors. Loads only adapter weights (optimizer/scheduler/step reset to zero) — use this to keep fine-tuning a finished LoRA. For full state resume (optimizer etc.) use save_state_on_train_end instead. Leave empty for plain LoRA training.
dim_from_weights: Read network_dim from the warm-start checkpoint instead of the form value. Set together with network_weights so rank matches the warm-start LoRA.
learning_rate: Base learning rate for the optimizer. Typical: 1e-5 to 1e-4 (1e-4 means 0.0001, 1e-5 means 0.00001).
max_train_epochs: Total training epochs. One epoch = one full pass through the dataset.
save_every_n_epochs: Save a checkpoint every N epochs. Set equal to max_train_epochs to save only the final model.
checkpointing_epochs: Save resumable training state every N epochs. State files are large; use a larger interval than save_every_n_epochs.
save_state_on_train_end: On normal training completion, write a full resumable state (<output_name>-state/, incl. optimizer/scheduler) so the run can be continued later. The next launch auto-detects it and offers to resume. Use with a larger max_train_epochs to keep training past a finished run. Produces large files.
gradient_accumulation_steps: Accumulate gradients over N steps before updating. Effective batch size = batch_size × accumulation_steps.
use_shuffled_caption_variants: Consume preprocessed caption-shuffle variants from the text-encoder cache. When the cache holds multiple variants, a random one is drawn per sample. Falls back silently to single-variant if no variants were preprocessed.
caption_dropout_rate: Probability per sample of dropping the caption (replaced with empty text embedding). Pushes the LoRA toward an unconditional bias — useful for style training where you want the look to apply regardless of prompt. Typical: 0.0–0.05 for character/concept LoRAs, 0.1–0.25 for style LoRAs (그림체 학습). Too high can blur prompt-driven diversity (pose/composition).
optimizer_type: Optimizer algorithm. AdamW8bit: memory-efficient 8-bit Adam. Others: AdamW, Lion, Prodigy, etc.
lr_scheduler: Learning rate schedule. constant: fixed LR. Others: cosine, cosine_with_restarts, polynomial.
timestep_sampling: How denoising timesteps are sampled during training. sigmoid: biased toward middle timesteps (recommended for flow matching).
discrete_flow_shift: Flow-matching shift parameter controlling the noise schedule distribution. Default: 1.0.
attn_mode: Attention backend. flash4: FlashAttention-4 (Linux, fastest). flash: FlashAttention-2. flex: PyTorch flex attention (cross-platform).
gradient_checkpointing: Recompute activations during backward pass instead of storing them. Trades compute for VRAM. Essential for low-VRAM setups.
unsloth_offload_checkpointing: Offload gradient checkpoints to CPU RAM. Further VRAM reduction at cost of speed. Requires gradient_checkpointing=true.
activation_memory_budget: torch.compile activation-memory budget (0-1): fraction of activations the partitioner may keep saved-for-backward before it starts recomputing. Lower = less VRAM, more recompute. 0.99 ≈ no recompute; 0.85 ≈ old peak at matched step time. Auto-skipped when gradient_checkpointing=true (incompatible/redundant).
blocks_to_swap: Number of DiT blocks to swap between GPU and CPU. 0: all on GPU. Higher values = more CPU offloading for low VRAM.
torch_compile: Enable torch.compile for the forward pass. Faster training after initial compilation. Compiles each DiT block at native shapes — one graph per token-count bucket family, no static padding.
cache_llm_adapter_outputs: Cache the LLM adapter layer outputs to disk. Avoids recomputing text encoder projections each epoch.
masked_loss: Apply loss only to non-masked regions (e.g., exclude text bubbles). Requires mask files in post_image_dataset/masks/ (or legacy masks/merged/) — run `make mask` to generate them.
mixed_precision: Mixed precision mode. bf16: recommended for modern GPUs. fp16: for older GPUs without bf16 support.
vae_chunk_size: VAE decoding chunk size. Larger = faster but more VRAM. 64 is a good balance.
vae_disable_cache: Disable VAE's internal KV cache. Reduces VRAM during VAE encoding/decoding.
use_vae_cache: Cache VAE-encoded latents to disk and read them during training. Avoids re-encoding images every epoch. Turn off for live VAE encoding (e.g. IP-Adapter live mode).
use_text_cache: Cache text encoder outputs to disk. Essential for lazy loading: encode → cache → free encoder → load DiT. Turn off for live text encoding.
skip_cache_check: Skip validation of cached files on startup. Faster startup when caches are known to be valid.
use_cmmd: Use CMMD (PE-Core MMD²) as the validation signal. Off by default in the GUI — CMMD adds the PE encoder + a sampling pass per held-out item, which costs extra VRAM and time. Off → falls back to the cheaper per-σ FM-MSE val pass (uninformative on Anima but free).
use_valid: Hold out a small validation slice from the training set (16 images by default — pinned via base.toml's validation_split_num). When off, the whole pool is used for training and no validation pass runs — skips the FM-MSE / CMMD eval and lets very small datasets train without losing samples. Writes/strips a {validation_split_num = 0, validation_split = 0.0} override on the variant's [[datasets]] block; base.toml is not touched.
validation_split_num: How many images to hold out for validation when 'use_valid' is on. Base.toml ships 16 — large enough for stable paired CMMD, small enough to barely dent the train pool. Bigger values give a quieter CMMD curve at the cost of fewer training samples and a slower val pass. Ignored when 'use_valid' is off (the zero-override wins). Writes/strips a {validation_split_num = N} override on the variant's [[datasets]] block; matching base.toml's value strips the override so base wins.
repeat_by_folder_name: Kohya-style folder repeats. When on, images inside a subfolder named {n}_... (e.g. image_dataset/5_mychar/) are repeated n times per epoch instead of num_repeats; a 0_... folder is excluded from training. Folder names survive preprocessing (resize/caches mirror the source tree), so this works on the resized tree too. Affects only the training pool — validation always uses 1 repeat. Writes/strips a repeat_by_folder_name override on the variant's [[datasets]] block; base.toml is not touched.
pretrained_model_name_or_path: Path to the base DiT model weights (.safetensors).
qwen3: Path to the Qwen3 text encoder weights for text-to-image conditioning.
vae: Path to the VAE model for image encoding/decoding.
output_dir: Base directory for trained LoRA checkpoints. With path_scope set, the GUI appends the scope at submit time, e.g. output/ckpt + data_group1 becomes output/ckpt/data_group1.
output_name: Base filename for saved checkpoints inside output_dir. Epoch/version suffixes are appended automatically.
training_comment: Free-text note embedded verbatim in the checkpoint metadata (ss_training_comment). Use it for training notes, dataset provenance, or technique variants. Leave empty for none.
source_image_dir: Base directory for raw images and .txt captions. With path_scope set, the GUI appends the scope before running preprocess, e.g. image_dataset + data_group1 becomes image_dataset/data_group1.
resized_image_dir: Base directory where preprocess writes resized PNGs. With path_scope set, the GUI appends the same scope used by source_image_dir, so resized images stay grouped with their source dataset.
lora_cache_dir: Base directory where preprocess writes VAE latent (.npz) and text-encoder (_anima_te.safetensors) caches. Training reads this as the dataset cache_dir. With path_scope set, the GUI appends the same scope.
path_scope: GUI-only dataset path scope. Set this to a dataset group such as `data_group1` to keep source images, resized images, LoRA caches, and checkpoints under matching subfolders. It is expanded into concrete paths when the GUI submits a job, then removed from the training snapshot. Leave blank if the paths already point at the exact folders you want.
path_pattern: Training filter applied after path_scope, relative to the scoped image/cache directory. Use it to train only part of a prepared dataset without changing where files are stored. Examples: with path_scope=data_group1, `*` trains everything under data_group1, `1/*` trains only data_group1/1, and `1/*|2/*` trains both subfolders.
preprocess_path_pattern: GUI-only preprocess filter. path_scope is applied first. For example, path_scope=data_group1 expands source_image_dir to image_dataset/data_group1 at GUI submit time, then this filter is matched relative to that root. `1/*` resizes/caches only image_dataset/data_group1/1 while preserving the output layout under post_image_dataset/resized/data_group1/1 and post_image_dataset/lora/data_group1/1. `*` processes everything; `1/*|2/*` OR-combines subfolders. This is separate from the training `path_pattern`; it only limits which images are preprocessed.
drop_lowres_images: When true, the preprocess auto-chain skips source images below the `min_pixels` threshold so they never enter the resize / VAE / TE caches. Applied to both preprocess/resize_images.py and preprocess/cache_text_embeddings.py via the same `--min_pixels` argument. Uncheck to keep every image regardless of size.
min_pixels: Pixel-count threshold used by `drop_lowres_images` (default 500_000 = 0.5MP). Forwarded verbatim to preprocess/resize_images.py and cache_text_embeddings.py as `--min_pixels`. Ignored when `drop_lowres_images = false`. Set to 0 (with the flag on) to disable the filter without flipping the checkbox.
batch_size: Number of images per training step, drawn from a single aspect-ratio bucket. Larger batches speed up training but increase VRAM usage; 1–4 recommended for 8 GB GPUs. Writes/strips a batch_size override on the variant's [[datasets]] block; matching base.toml's value strips the override so base wins.
num_repeats: How many times each image is repeated per epoch. 1 = each image trains once; increasing it effectively augments a small dataset but multiplies steps-per-epoch linearly. Writes/strips a num_repeats override on the variant's [[datasets.subsets]] block; matching base.toml's value strips the override so base wins.
sample_ratio: Sub-sample ratio for the training set (0.0–1.0). 1.0 = all images, 0.5 = half, 0.1 = 10%. Presets like half/quarter/tenth/debug set this <1.0 for quick iteration — restore to 1.0 for real training. Writes/strips a sample_ratio override on the variant's [[datasets.subsets]] block; matching base.toml's value strips the override so base wins.
sample_prompts: Preview prompts to render so you can watch for overfitting by eye — independent of validation/CMMD. One prompt per line. Each sample is staged as a latent first; sample_decode_inline controls when it is decoded to PNG, and any latent not decoded successfully during training is retried at the end. A prompt with no explicit seed uses a fixed per-prompt seed so the same prompt renders from identical noise every epoch (comparable gallery). Leave empty to disable. Per-line modifiers are supported, e.g. '1girl, solo --w 832 --h 1216 --s 28 --d 42 --l 4.0' (w/h = size, s = steps, d = seed, l = CFG scale, n = negative prompt).
sample_every_n_epochs: Capture the sample prompts every N epochs; 0 = disabled. Pair with sample_prompts. Sampling is independent of use_valid. Each latent is saved first and sample_decode_inline controls when it is decoded. Use a small dataset-appropriate value (e.g. 1–4) to get a per-epoch gallery for spotting where quality peaks before overfitting.
sample_decode_inline: Controls when training-sample latents are decoded to PNG. auto (recommended): decode after every sampling event when blocks_to_swap=0, or defer to the end of training when blocks_to_swap>0; true forces immediate decode; false always defers. Immediate decode temporarily moves the DiT and network to CPU before moving the VAE to GPU. On OOM or failure, the latent is kept and retried at the end. This setting does not enable sampling and does not suppress the final decode.
sample_at_first: Also render the sample prompts once before training starts (epoch 0) — a baseline of the un-tuned model to compare later epochs against.
use_easycontrol: Enable EasyControl extended self-attention image conditioning. Frozen DiT with per-block cond LoRA + scalar bias b_cond. Requires reference images in easycontrol-dataset/.
easycontrol_drop_p: CFG dropout probability for EasyControl image conditioning. Each batch drops the condition entirely with this probability (falling back to baseline DiT behavior), enabling independent image-CFG and text-CFG at inference. Typical: 0.05–0.2.
easycontrol_cond_noise_max: Max std-dev of Gaussian noise added to the cond latent during training. Per-step σ ~ U(0, max), applied as cond + σ·ε. 0.0 = no noise (ref==target identity); positive values (e.g. 0.3) degrade cond from 'perfect blueprint' to 'lossy hint', forcing text to carry residual high-frequency detail. Inference uses clean cond unaffected.
cond_res_scale: EasyControl Position-Aware Interpolation (PAI) scale. <1.0 downsamples the cond stream to this ratio (cond stream only; target + loss stay full-res) and interpolates cond RoPE positions back onto the target grid for spatial alignment. 1.0 = no scaling (default). 0.5 ≈ 4× fewer cond tokens, ~25-30% training speedup. Good for subject/semantic control (identity, objects); keep at 1.0 for structure-critical tasks (lineart colorize).
